  4)              Write the significance of knowledge representation. Apply knowledge representation to  
  convert the following sentences into well-formed formulas:  
  
  A)            1. Marcus was a man.  
  2. Marcus was a Pompeian.  
  3. All Pompeian were Romans.  
  4. Caeser was a ruler.                                                                (5)  
  5. All Romans were either loyal to Caeser or hated him.  
  6. Everyone is loyal to someone.  
  7. People only try to assassinate rulers they are not loyal to.  
  8. Marcus tried to assassinate Caeser.  
  9. All men are people.  
  
  
  B)         Prove the following sentences using First Order Logic and Forward Reasoning using the  
  above nine well-formed formulas given in question 4(a):  
  
  1. Was Marcus loyal to Caeser?                                                        (5)  
  2. Was Marcus hates Caeser?  
  
  
  5)              Explain the difference between syntax and semantics in First-Order Logic (FOL).  
  Provide an example of a First-Order Logic statement and describe both its syntactic  
  (5)  
  structure and its semantic meaning.  
  A)  
  B)         You have been planning a picnic for your family. You are trying to decide whether to  
  postpone due to rain. The chance of rain on any day is 15%. The morning of the picnic is  
  cloudy. The probability of it being cloudy is 25% and on days where it rains, its cloudy (5)  
  in the morning 80% of the time. Calculate the postponement of the picnic by using  
  Baye's Theorem.
